subject: Linguistics
title: Descriptive Versus Prescriptive Grammar
description: A 60-second lesson on Descriptive Versus Prescriptive Grammar.

hook.text: 'Who did you go with?' Teachers call that wrong. Linguists call it standard spoken English.

buildup.text: Prescriptive grammar tells you what to say; descriptive grammar records what people actually say.

discovery.text: Linguists focus on descriptive grammar because it reveals the real system operating in speakers' minds.

twist.text: Many prescriptive rules were invented in the 1700s by imitating Latin—not from English usage.

climax.text: Ending a sentence with a preposition? Churchill reportedly mocked that rule as absurd.

punchline.text: Grammar is what speakers do, not what books demand.

quiz.question: What does descriptive grammar focus on?
